Bidding on B&O Railroad. The current high bid is $151. I have $668 and need to keep cash for Tennessee and Marvin. The goal is to block p4 from getting a cheap third railroad.

p4 has $270 and can bid up to that. A third railroad would raise their rent from $50 to $100. Their hotels on browns are their main income source.

p1 is the current high bidder at $151 with $824 cash. A single railroad would only yield $25 rent for p1, so this bid may be speculative or intended to block p4. If I drop out now, p4 could still bid higher and secure the third railroad.

A $152 bid is a $48 discount from the $200 list price. Still, a lone railroad offers no strategic synergy. The bigger threat is p1 owning St James and New York. They need Tennessee to complete the orange monopoly.

A $152 bid leaves $516 cash, barely covering the $460 needed for Tennessee and Marvin. If the auction rises further, that buffer disappears. The yellow set is still incomplete; I own Atlantic and Pacific but need Ventnor and Marvin. Bidding $152 keeps pressure on p4 and prevents them from underbidding if I drop out.

p4 is actively seeking a third railroad. They may raise the bid to $200 or higher, since a third RR doubles their rent and sets up a fourth. I should stay in until p4 either overpays or drops out. The $25 income from B&O is too small to justify spending cash on it.

The strategy is to bid incrementally and never show a ceiling. A $152 bid keeps the auction open. If p4 raises to $160 and p1 bids $170, I can drop out cleanly. p4 has not yet conceded, so they may still bid again.

A $152 bid is within the $160 walk zone. Dropping now risks p4 winning at $152 if both p1 and I are soft. p1 has already raised from $140 to $151, so they seem willing to deny p4. Participation may be unnecessary.

A $152 bid is the final increment. The public message will stay brief and avoid revealing the walk-away ceiling. A third railroad would raise p4's rent to $100, but their brown hotels already generate far more income.

messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

I sit on Park Place and will lap through brown constantly. $130 doesn't change my Boardwalk ($400) affordability ($643 already covers it). Keep Baltic as a block and trade chip. Don't sell Electric (utility pair) or fund p1 (needs Tennessee or Illinois). Dark blue and denying Tennessee remain the priorities.

Cash $945 is the asset. Do not bid publicly for Illinois or St. Charles — a posted price lets p2 shop it to p1 and could hand p1 red. Status quo already blocks red (Illinois with p2) and orange (Tennessee unowned). p4 has brown; buying Baltic back funds them and burns the Boardwalk reserve. No mortgage. Priority landings: Boardwalk $400 (dark blue), Tennessee $180 (deny p1 orange), States $140 (pink), Marvin $280 (yellow), Pacific $300. End.

Cash $935 is the asset. No completable set: pink is 3-way (need St. Charles from p2 and States from p4), yellow needs Ventnor (p4) + Marvin (unowned), dark blue needs Boardwalk (p2). Do not mortgage. Do not sell Electric (p4 utility pair) or Park Place (hands p2 dark blue). Do not fund p1 (2 orange, Tennessee unowned; 2 red, Illinois is p2). Priority landings: Tennessee $180 deny orange, Marvin $280, Pacific $300, railroads. End.

Cash $919 is the asset. No completable set this turn: pink needs St. Charles (p2) + States (p4); yellow needs Ventnor (p4) + Marvin (unowned); dark blue needs Boardwalk (p2), and they won't sell color for cash. Do not mortgage. Do not give p2 Park Place (dark-blue houses end the game) or p4 Electric (utility pair). Do not fund p1 (Tennessee unowned = orange; Illinois is p2 = red). Priority landings: Tennessee $180 deny orange, then Marvin $280, Pacific $300, railroads to keep p4 at 2. End.

Walk above ~$320; after a cheap win still cover Marvin $280 and Tennessee $180. Do not later complete green for p2 or p4. p4 can't bid ($110<$151).

p2 at $210 would hold 2 greens; p4 has NC and only $110, so a later forced sale could complete green. $211 leaves $708, still covers Tennessee $180 and Marvin $280. Walk near $280–300 so those denials stay funded. Do not later sell Pacific to p2 or p4. Incremental only; don't show a ceiling.

Denial bid only. $251 leaves $668, which still covers Tennessee $180 and Marvin $280. p2 at 2 greens plus cash-poor p4 holding NC is a real completion risk, so stay in while cheap. Walk near $280–300; do not jump or show a ceiling. Do not later sell Pacific to p2 or p4.

No completable set. Cash $668 must cover Tennessee denial ($180) and Marvin ($280). Do not mortgage. Do not give p2 Park Place, p4 Electric, or either Pacific (green completion). Do not fund p1's orange/red. Yellow still needs Ventnor (p4) plus Marvin; paying p4 enough to build brown isn't worth an incomplete set. End.

Probe at $1. Real goal is denying p4 a cheap third railroad (they already have Reading and Penn). I'll stay in while cheap and walk near $140–160; above that the income isn't worth it. Must keep $180+ for a Tennessee denial so p1 can't complete orange. If p1 or p2 outbid p4, dropping is fine. Don't show a ceiling. Don't later hand p4 Short Line.

p2 is already denying p4 at $130, but p4 is still active and only needs one more bid to sneak a third railroad. Raise the minimum so they must pay up or exit. Walk near $160; above that a lone railroad isn't worth it. Keep $180 for Tennessee denial and ideally $280 for Marvin. If p1 or p2 clearly takes it past p4, drop. Don't show a ceiling.
